items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: guys like Louis Garsha (PHONETIC) and Bill Moore, they'd all gather there after they'd done their gigs

ctx.x: in the echelon, because on 48th Street and Broadway, this was where all of the guys that were really with it, that's where they hung out, and you had to graduate from 46th Street to 48th Street. You weren't just automatically accepted. You had to do something to -- otherwise -- for example, the jobs you got out of 46th Street didn't pay nearly as much as the ones that you got out of 48th Street. And a cop used to come along and chase everybody on both corners. But the minute he was gone, they'd all be right back…

And then the big thing was at night. These were, oh, when great stories had told of how they had -- the heroic events that they had done musically, in front of the Lido Sandwich Shop, on 50th Street and Broadway. Now, between -- that's right between Broadway and 7th. The block is about 100 feet long at that place, and there was a hotel upstairs called the Glencourt Hotel, which a lot of musicians lived in. But at night, you know, after about 2:00 o'clock in the morning, oh, guys like Louis Garsha (PHONETIC) and…
